question: What does $26.27 per ADS imply about 2027 LEAP margins, CapEx intensity, and free cash flow conversion?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a cyclical manufacturer borrows heavily at peak CapEx, the market prices both the growth story and the balance-sheet risk.
epigraph.author: Howard Marks (adapted from cycle-valuation memos)

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $26.27, ASE Technology (NYSE: ASX) carries a $57.99 billion market cap on Finviz ($61.00 billion on TradingView) and a $68.08 billion enterprise value [13, 14]. On trailing figures, shares trade at 24.90x P/E on $1.05 TTM EPS, 12.82x EV/EBITDA, 2.73x EV/Sales, and 4.35x P/B [13]. On Street screens, Finviz prints 12.72x forward P/E (~$2.07 implied consensus EPS) and a 2.47% estimated dividend yield ($0.65 per ADS) [13, 15]. That optical gap reflects rapid LEAP scaling from ~$1.6 billion in FY2025 toward >$4.0 billion in FY2026 [3, 13], alongside Q3 diluted EPS reaching US$0.365 per ADS ($1.46 annualized) [28].

Yet the stock fell -45.19% from its $47.93 52-week high, including a -37.63% 30-day slide on TradingView (-30.39% on Finviz) [13, 14]. Why did shares sell off so hard after Q3 2026 beat expectations (30.6% ATM gross margin) and October 2026 revenue surged +47.1% YoY to NT$88,615 million [1, 27]? Four Pass 1 discoveries explain the reset. First, 9M 2026 cash PP&E CapEx of NT$249,792 million drove free cash flow to -NT$115,929 million, forcing total debt up +53.9% to NT$406,461 million (0.66x net debt/equity) while CFO Joseph Tung guided 2027 CapEx even higher than $11.5B [3, 28, 29]. Second, Q3 net interest jumped to NT$2,611 million (~NT$10.4B annualized) ahead of a 2027 maturity wall [28, 30]. Third, the November 18, 2026 U.S. BIS AI export rule tightening narrowed OSAT license exemptions and clouded 2H 2027 AI visibility [33]. Fourth, 2027–2028 competition is intensifying as TSMC doubles CoWoS, Amkor builds its $12 billion CHIPS-subsidized Arizona site, and Intel EMIB-T wins dual-source validation [34, 35, 37].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: what $26.27 already bakes in

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF strips away price targets and asks what operating results justify a $68.08 billion enterprise value today. Note that Finviz still displays a stale 18.44x trailing P/FCF ratio, whereas audited Q3 2026 filings show -NT$115.9 billion of 9M 2026 cash burn [13, 28]. Equity buyers at $26.27 are therefore underwriting an aggressive 2028–2030 free cash flow recovery.

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF: What $26.27 ($68.08B EV) Prices In Over 10 Years (Nov 20, 2026)
rows: Needs LEAP ~$6.8B–$8B by 2027–2028 plus stable ATM/EMS growth [3, 13].
Requires ATM GM >=28% despite higher depreciation and ~2% Q4 EMS OM [2, 28].
Assumes CapEx cools from >35% of sales in FY26 back toward 16%–18%, though CFO guided 2027 CapEx higher [3, 6, 28].
Higher net debt (NT$406.5B gross), 3.04 1Y beta, and Taiwan/BIS risk [29, 33].
Prices a 2-turn OSAT upgrade, down from 12.82x TTM today [13, 18].
web_blocks.takeaway: At $26.27, ASX still requires 10.5x–11.5x steady-state EV/EBITDA and post-2027 FCF normalization; with 2027 CapEx guided above $11.5B, investors absorb multi-year cash burn before free cash flow recovers [3, 28].

web_blocks.title: Base-case earnings and FCF estimate for FY2027

web_blocks.html: Before ranking ASX against peers, we state our explicit FY2027 base-case earnings bridge. Rising depreciation, $340M of net interest, and EMS margin drag reconcile to a much lower GAAP ADS earnings figure than headline Street forward multiples imply.

web_blocks.the_number: $1.22 FY2027E EPS per ADS ($1.19 post-NCI) and $16.47 Base-Case Fair Value (13.5x Fwd P/E; ~9.0x EV/EBITDA)
web_blocks.how_calculated: Start with FY2026E revenue (~$26.5B) and model +14% FY2027 revenue growth to ~$30.2B as LEAP scales from >$4.0B to ~$6.8B. Apply a 12.2% consolidated operating margin ($3.68B EBIT) less $340M net interest ($3.34B PBT) and 19% effective tax ($2.71B consolidated net income) across 2.22B diluted ADS shares to yield $1.22 EPS per ADS ($1.19 after ~2.7% USI Shanghai non-controlling interest). Note that Finviz's 12.72x forward P/E at $26.27 implies ~$2.07 Street consensus EPS, which would require ~19% consolidated operating margins (implausible with ~40% EMS revenue near ~2% OM) or unadjusted share-count conventions; we use our reconciled $1.22 GAAP bridge and cap the Base multiple at 13.5x—below TSMC's 13.81x [20].
web_blocks.the_inputs: Q3 2026 consolidated GM (22.1%), ATM GM (30.6%), and Q3 diluted EPS (US$0.365/ADS) [28]; Oct 2026 revenue (+47.1% YoY) [27]; FY2026 CapEx ($11.5B, with 2027 guided higher) lifting annual D&A [3, 6]; Q3 net interest run rate (NT$2,611M/qtr) [28]; and 0.66x net debt/equity [29].
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case $12.00 (12.0x trough $1.00 EPS on $28.5B sales and 10.8% OPM if BIS curbs cut ATM GM to 23.5%); Base Case $16.47 (13.5x $1.22 EPS, -37.3% vs. CMP); Bull Case $28.00 (17.5x $1.60 EPS on $32.5B sales and ~14.4% OPM if LEAP hits ~$8B and FCF inflects in 2H27).
web_blocks.if_off: Every 100 bps slip in consolidated operating margin cuts ~$0.11 from FY2027E EPS ($30.2B x 1% x 0.81 / 2.22B). If FY2027 CapEx exceeds $11.5B without positive 2H27 FCF, the multiple compresses toward Amkor at 10.0x–11.0x ($11.55–$13.42) rather than holding 13.5x.

web_blocks.title: Cross-border peer valuation and Stage 4 sector reset

web_blocks.html: All five semiconductor packaging, foundry, and EMS peers dropped into Stage 4 during the November 2026 hardware selloff. That group-wide repricing sets a strict valuation ceiling for ASX.

web_blocks.caption: Cross-Border Valuation & Quality Comps: OSAT, Foundry-Packaging & EMS Peers (Nov 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: After the November selloff, TSM trades at 13.81x forward P/E with 32.67% ROIC and 57.8% OPM, leaving ASX (12.72x headline forward P/E, 21.5x our reconciled $1.22 FY27E EPS, 10.28% ROIC) expensive relative to both TSMC and Amkor (10.96x) [13, 19, 20].

web_blocks.mechanism: As a premier supplier of high-layer ABF substrates for AI GPUs and servers, Ibiden launched a multi-year CapEx wave (¥120B–¥200B+ per year) that turned free cash flow negative and compressed ROIC even as AI mix expanded.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Ibiden rallied >3x from 2020 to its 2023 peak (~¥9,500) at >30x forward P/E, then dropped >35% during 2024 digestion quarters when utilization dipped and new depreciation hit the P&L.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Forward P/E looks deceptively cheap during a CapEx supercycle, yet high fixed depreciation triggers 30%–45% drawdowns whenever export rules or hyperscaler orders create utilization uncertainty.

web_blocks.html: Comparing ASX to Amkor Technology (AMKR) and TSMC (TSM) explains why we cap ASE's Base multiple at 13.5x rather than paying a premium. Amkor ($7.49 billion market cap) trades at 10.96x forward P/E and 5.48x EV/EBITDA, aided by CHIPS grants and a 35% U.S. investment tax credit on its $12 billion Arizona plan [19, 35, 37]. ASX merits a modest premium to Amkor due to 4x scale and 30.6% ATM gross margin [2, 13, 19]. Yet TSMC now trades at 13.81x forward P/E and 13.70x EV/EBITDA while delivering 3.2x higher ROIC (32.67% vs. 10.28%) and 5x higher operating margin (57.78% vs. 11.46%) [13, 20]. Paying more than TSMC's 13.81x multiple for an OSAT with negative FCF and 91.3% external substrate reliance is indefensible. Meanwhile, EMS peers Jabil (JBL) at 10.24x and Celestica (CLS) at 9.09x forward P/E earn higher ROIC (19.83% and 17.41%) than ASE's consolidated 10.28% [13, 25, 26]. At $26.27, ASX trades at 21.5x our reconciled $1.22 FY27E EPS—well above our 13.5x cap.

web_blocks.caption: 12–18 Month Scenario Valuation Matrix (Reconciled GAAP Bridge & Peer-Capped Multiples)
rows: Bear Case (BIS Curb / AI Pause, 10.8% OPM / 23.5% ATM GM)
Amkor-Parity Stress Case (LEAP $5.4B, Base cut to 11.0x)
web_blocks.takeaway: Reconciling the FY2027E bridge ($1.22 EPS) and capping the Base multiple at 13.5x (below TSMC's 13.81x) yields a $16.47 Base fair value (-37.3% vs. $26.27) and a $17.44 expected value (-33.6%); under the Amkor-parity stress test ($11.55), stressed expected value falls to $14.98 (-43.0%).

web_blocks.html: What Would Change This Valuation Call: Fair value would reset toward $12.00 if BIS export curbs slow 2H 2027 AI runs or ATM gross margin slips below 26%. A sustained move above $28.00 requires 2027 LEAP revenue tracking >$8.0 billion, consolidated OPM holding >14.5%, and positive 2H 2027 free cash flow [3, 28, 33].

book_paragraphs: With Chapters 1 through 6 locked and audited, let us open the November 20, 2026 market ledger and confront the single most important question on ASX today. At $26.27 per ADS, why did a company whose October sales just jumped 47.1 percent lose nearly 38 percent of its market value in thirty days, and does $26.27 offer genuine value or remain overpriced on reconciled cash earnings?

On the surface, a trailing screen makes ASE look deceptively tidy. At $26.27, the market capitalization stands at $57.99 billion on Finviz ($61.00 billion on TradingView), with an enterprise value of $68.08 billion. Trailing earnings put the stock at 24.90 times P/E and 12.82 times EV/EBITDA, while headline Wall Street consensus prints 12.72 times forward earnings with a 2.47 percent estimated dividend yield.

So why did institutions dump the stock from $47.93 down to $26.27—a brutal 45.2 percent drawdown from its 52-week high? Because professional hardware investors read cash-flow footnotes and export notices, not just headline P/E ratios. Across Chapters 3 through 6, our blind audit uncovered four heavy weights that hit the valuation multiple at the exact moment broader semiconductor sentiment cracked.

First, the Q3 2026 Form 6-K showed that 9M 2026 capital expenditures reached NT$249.8 billion, driving free cash flow to negative NT$115.9 billion and forcing ASE to borrow NT$140.9 billion net. Total interest-bearing debt jumped 53.9 percent in nine months to NT$406.5 billion, pushing net debt-to-equity to 0.66 times and lifting Q3 net interest expense to NT$2.61 billion—more than a NT$10 billion annualized interest bill. Worse, CFO Joseph Tung confirmed on October 29 that 2027 CapEx will be even larger than 2026's $11.5 billion.

Second, Finviz still prints an 18.44 times price-to-free-cash-flow ratio from stale trailing data, masking the reality that ASE is burning roughly $3.6 billion of cash through September 2026 to build cleanrooms. Third, on November 18, 2026, the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security tightened AI chip export rules and narrowed OSAT license exemptions, casting doubt on 2H 2027 shipments for a firm with 89.2 percent of its non-current assets in Taiwan and China. Fourth, 2027–2028 competitive capacity is rising fast: TSMC plans to double internal CoWoS capacity, Amkor is scaling a $12 billion CHIPS-subsidized Arizona campus, and Intel EMIB-T won dual-source validation at MediaTek.

Let us run a clean Reverse DCF to see what $26.27 still assumes. At a $68.08 billion enterprise value, the market has pulled back its heroic assumptions from three weeks ago, yet $26.27 still implies roughly 9 percent to 10.5 percent ten-year revenue compounding, 12 percent to 13 percent terminal operating margins, and 8 percent to 9.5 percent normalized free cash flow margins once CapEx cools after 2027.

Notice the catch in that Reverse DCF: even at $26.27, ASX trades at roughly 10.5x to 11.5x implied steady-state EV/EBITDA—still two turns above its historical 6.5x to 9.5x OSAT range—and assumes a higher 10 percent to 10.5 percent cost of capital because of its new debt load and geopolitical concentration. Meanwhile, look across the peer table on November 20, 2026. Every single hardware peer—Amkor, TSMC, Jabil, and Celestica—fell into Stage 4 alongside ASX.

And here is the comparison that stops any rushed value pitch cold: TSMC itself dropped to 13.81 times forward earnings and 13.70 times EV/EBITDA. TSMC earns a 32.67 percent return on invested capital and a 57.78 percent operating margin with a near-monopoly on 2nm and 3nm silicon. ASE earns a 10.28 percent ROIC and an 11.46 percent operating margin, relies on external vendors for 91.3 percent of its IC substrates, and still carries a 40 percent EMS business guiding to 2 percent operating margins in Q4. We must never value ASE at a higher multiple than TSMC.

Now walk carefully through the exact arithmetic of our FY2027 earnings bridge, because rigorous math changes everything. Start with $26.5 billion of FY2026 revenue and grow 14 percent to $30.2 billion in FY2027 as LEAP rises toward $6.8 billion. Apply a 12.2 percent consolidated operating margin to get $3.68 billion in EBIT. Subtract $340 million of net interest to reach $3.34 billion in pretax profit, apply a 19 percent tax rate to reach $2.71 billion in net income, and divide by 2.22 billion diluted ADS shares. That yields exactly $1.22 per ADS ($1.19 after minority leakage)—not the ~$2.07 implied by Street screens.

Capping ASE's multiple at 13.5x—just beneath TSMC's 13.81x—on $1.22 of reconciled FY2027 earnings puts our Base fair value at $16.47, which is 37.3 percent below today's $26.27 close. Even our Bull Case ($1.60 EPS at 17.5x if LEAP reaches $8 billion and FCF turns positive) reaches only $28.00 (+6.6 percent), while our Bear Case ($1.00 EPS at 12.0x) sits at $12.00. Weighting 20 percent Bull, 50 percent Base, and 30 percent Bear yields an expected value of $17.44 (-33.6 percent), and cutting the Base multiple to Amkor parity (11.0x on $1.05 EPS = $11.55) lowers stressed expected value to $14.98 (-43.0 percent). At $26.27, ASX is overvalued on reconciled earnings as well as broken on the chart.

book_subsections.title: The Depreciation Cliff and Balance-Sheet Hurdle for 2027
paragraphs: When an industrial company commits $11.5 billion in capital spending in a single year—and CFO Joseph Tung warns that 2027 CapEx will be even larger—accounting depreciation lags cash outflows by four to six quarters. In Q3 2026, quarterly depreciation and amortization already reached NT$22.26 billion, an annualized run rate near NT$89 billion. As 13 new fab builds and 8 expansions come online through 2027, annual depreciation will step up sharply regardless of quarterly fab utilization.

That fixed-cost staircase explains the Ibiden Co., Ltd. parallel from 2021–2024. During the ABF substrate boom, Ibiden looked cheap on forward P/E right up until customer digestion quarters collided with peak depreciation, knocking the stock down more than 35 percent. For ASE, any 2H 2027 export pause or customer dual-sourcing to Amkor Arizona or Intel EMIB-T turns operating leverage sharply in reverse, especially with NT$155.2 billion of long-term debt maturing inside one to three years.

book_subsections.title: Why Peer Gravity Keeps New Capital Sidelined Even After a 45% Drop
paragraphs: Many investors assume a 45 percent pullback automatically creates deep value. In cyclical semiconductors, however, valuation floors depend on peer compression and reconciled free-cash-flow yield. Today, Amkor trades at 5.48 times EV/EBITDA and 10.96 times forward earnings while enjoying U.S. CHIPS subsidies and a 35 percent investment tax credit that lower its net capital burden.

Even more telling, EMS leaders Jabil (10.24x forward P/E) and Celestica (9.09x forward P/E) trade at single-digit or low-double-digit forward multiples despite generating 17 percent to 20 percent ROIC. At $26.27, ASX trades at 21.5 times our reconciled $1.22 FY2027E EPS—well above TSMC at 13.81x. Only inside a $14.00 to $16.00 watch zone (11.5x to 13.1x reconciled EPS, just above the $13.35–$13.71 52-week low) would valuation begin to offer a real margin of safety.

book_subsections.title: Currency Swaps, Customer Deposits, and the Stale P/FCF Screen Trap
paragraphs: Two subtle accounting items explain why automated valuation screens mislead investors on ASX today. First, popular financial portals still print an 18.44 times price-to-free-cash-flow ratio based on lagged trailing quarters, giving value hunters the false impression that ASE generates roughly $3 billion of annual free cash flow. In reality, the audited cash-flow statement in the Q3 2026 Form 6-K proves ASE spent NT$249.8 billion on cash property, plant, and equipment against NT$133.9 billion of operating cash flow across the first nine months of 2026—a cash deficit of NT$115.9 billion, or roughly $3.6 billion U.S. dollars.

Second, ASE carries NT$109.2 billion in non-current other liabilities by September 30, 2026—driven heavily by customer capacity advance deposits under Note 37(e)—and recognized NT$7.8 billion of non-operating derivative and financial-asset gains in nine-month earnings alongside US$4.30 billion of currency swaps. Customer deposits are a genuine vote of confidence from hyperscalers, yet they are liabilities tied to cleanroom delivery schedules, while derivative mark-to-market gains can reverse whenever USD/NTD exchange rates shift.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Always check the P&L arithmetic yourself. Once $30.2B revenue at 12.2% OPM yields $1.22 EPS—not $2.00—and TSMC sits at 13.8x, a 13.5x cap puts ASX Base fair value at $16.47 (-37% below $26.27), proving the stock is both fundamentally expensive and technically broken.
